svg.title: SVG + base64: encoding is not a security boundary
svg.desc: How an SVG file travels as base64, where it can run code, what TLS, Cloudflare, CORS, Xano, Elm and Rust each check along the request path, and definitions of base64, compiling, machine code and bare metal, TLS hop by hop across Next.js hydration and a CRM to Shopify data bus, JVM, iPaaS (SAP, Azure, Celigo, Magento) and Wasm stacks with Consent Mode v2 and idempotency keys, VM versus Docker and Kubernetes isolation and transport, and thirty-one security gaps with the control that closes each.
svg.text: SVG + BASE64 — ENCODING IS NOT A SECURITY BOUNDARY
Dashed = a gap, not a design. Numbers match the list below.
ONE SVG, THREE WAYS IN — SAME BYTES, DIFFERENT RISK
1 · Source SVG: what the file says
SVG is XML: it can run code and carry data, not just pixels.
2 · Base64 data URI: how it travels
· Same bytes, new alphabet: about 33% larger.
· Anyone decodes it in one line: atob(s).
· “<script” is no longer visible to a text filter.
· Not encrypted, not signed, not validated.
3 · How it's rendered decides if it runs
Static image. Script does not run.
Text and metadata are still readable.
cookies, tokens, PHI on the page.
Script RUNS in the file's origin.
FOUR WORDS THAT GET CONFUSED — ONLY ONE OF THEM CHANGES WHAT CODE CAN DO
Rewrites any bytes as 64 text characters.
Never fails, never checks, never hides.
Rust compiles to machine code or Wasm · Elm to JS
Translates source into a different program.
One-way: comments and names are gone.
Binary instructions: an opcode plus operands,
specific to one chip family (x86-64, ARM64).
Not secret: objdump or Ghidra reads it back.
Code runs straight on the hardware: firmware,
process isolation, no OS to contain a bug.
Bare metal is dashed: a memory bug there owns the whole device, so Rust memory safety and signed firmware (secure boot) carry all the weight.
THE REQUEST PATH — WHAT EACH LAYER CHECKS, AND WHAT IT DOESN'T
pure view can't fetch or store
ports are the only exit to JS
opaque types mask PII on screen
a user editing the compiled JS
prove the rule is the right one
types force a check, not a policy
TLS PROTECTS EACH HOP, NOT THE DATA — EVERY BOX BELOW DECRYPTS IT
A · Next.js compile: server render, then CSR hydration
TLS ends; HTML may be cached
HTML + RSC payload carry the props
readable in View Source and caches
event row waits for the processor
transforms; reads Admin token from KV
plaintext: in memory, in logs if printed
must verify HMAC on the raw body
Each arrow is its own TLS session. Data is plaintext inside every box, so anything stored, cached, logged or rendered there is outside TLS's protection.
SAME DATA, THREE STACKS — JVM MIDDLEWARE vs IPAAS vs WASM, WITH CONSENT MODE V2 AND IDEMPOTENCY KEYS
C · JVM stack: Salesforce, MuleSoft and Salesforce Commerce Cloud, feeding Google Merchant
governor limits bound each tenant; you can't patch it
Java on the JVM; DataWeave transforms payloads
JavaScript on Rhino, running inside the JVM
one process sees all order and customer data
consent state is often lost in the transforms
D · iPaaS stack: from SAP through Azure and Celigo to Magento (Adobe Commerce)
IDoc, BAPI/RFC and OData out of the ERP
integration users often hold broad roles
Key Vault + managed identity, not keys in config
SaaS flows map and transform each record
plaintext: retries and error records keep payloads
PHP; REST, GraphQL and RabbitMQ queues
checkout JavaScript is the Magecart target
E · Wasm stack: from Shopify through a Cloudflare Worker and a Shopify Function to Google Merchant
captures Consent Mode v2 at the storefront
V8 isolate; consent gate before egress
Shopify Function · Rust compiled to Wasm
no network, no files, an instruction limit
GraphQL input in, a list of operations out
product upsert by offerId: a retry overwrites
Shared JVM process; quotas and governor limits
Vendor tenancy: your data on Celigo's platform
Own memory per module; a V8 isolate per Worker
Any library in the process can connect out
Flows reach every connected system's API
Functions: none. Workers: fetch via the host
Garbage-collected; secret Strings can't be wiped
PHP and ABAP are memory-safe; risk is config
Can't touch host memory; Rust ownership inside
Small modules; risk sits in the host imports
You: SAP Notes, Magento patches. Celigo: vendor
Shopify and Cloudflare; you rebuild the module
Must survive every DataWeave map and job
The ERP has no consent field: map it or lose it
Captured at the storefront, checked at the edge
Service Bus duplicate detection; IDoc numbers
Event ID deduped in a Durable Object
Wasm doesn't make data private; it limits what code can reach. Consent and idempotency are data rules, so every stack must carry them with every event.
ISOLATION AND TRANSPORT — A VM vs DOCKER vs KUBERNETES: WHERE THE WALL IS, AND HOW DATA CROSSES IT
each guest boots its own kernel
a process on the host's kernel
Escape needs a hypervisor bug: rare and high value.
The host can still read guest memory unless it's a
One shared host kernel: the only wall
Escape needs one kernel bug, --privileged, or a
mounted docker.sock. Root on the host sees every container.
ENV and COPY .env stay in image layers: docker history.
Pod to pod, across nodes: plaintext by default, and
any pod can reach any pod until a NetworkPolicy says no.
Secrets are base64, not encrypted, unless etcd encryption is on.
Shared host kernel: namespaces, cgroups, seccomp
Docker's wall per node, plus RBAC on the API
A kernel bug, --privileged or a mounted docker.sock
Any container escape, or a token with broad RBAC
Over the VPC; not always encrypted
Host bridge network: plaintext between containers
Flat network: any pod reaches any pod, in plaintext
TLS, WireGuard or IPsec between VMs
TLS inside each app; host root can still sniff
mTLS mesh (Istio, Linkerd) or WireGuard (Cilium, Calico)
Cloud KMS or a vault; disk encryption
Never in ENV or image layers; mount at runtime
Encrypt etcd with a KMS provider; prefer a vault
Host can read it, unless a confidential VM
Host root and any privileged container
The node, and anyone allowed to exec into the pod
A VM is the stronger wall; a container is the faster one. Neither encrypts data on the wire: TLS, mTLS or WireGuard does that, one hop at a time.
THIRTY-ONE GAPS — AND THE CONTROL THAT CLOSES EACH
Anyone reverses it with atob() or base64 -d.
Fix: Encrypt or tokenize. Never base64 a secret, API key, token or card number and call it hidden.
A WAF or scanner looking for “<script” misses it inside base64.
Fix: Decode first, then sanitize: DOMPurify or svgo, stripping script, on* handlers, foreignObject, external href.
innerHTML, inline <svg>, <object>, <iframe> and same-origin uploads all run script.
Fix: Render untrusted SVG with . Send CSP: sandbox on .svg. Serve uploads from a separate asset domain.
Browsers honor it. curl, servers and AI agents ignore it.
Fix: Authorize every request server-side, per record, in Xano or the Worker. Deny by default.
Cloudflare terminates TLS; Flexible mode sends plain HTTP to the origin.
Fix: Use Full (strict). Sign a BAA before any PHI. Encrypt sensitive fields before they reach the edge.
Xano request history and Cloudflare logs can store full request bodies.
Fix: Scrub fields or disable body logging. In Rust, Pii<T> redacts in Debug and refuses to serialize.
SVG carries data, not just pixels
<text>, <metadata> and XMP hold names and IDs. A chart of patient data is PHI.
Fix: Strip metadata on export. Classify an exported SVG as the data it shows, with the same retention.
Elm prevents your own bugs, not an attacker editing the JavaScript.
Fix: Enforce every rule again on the server. Treat Elm and Rust types as a second line, not the first.
Machine code disassembles and Elm output is readable JS. Keys shipped in either are public.
Fix: Keep secrets on the server or in a key vault. Ship only tokens that are scoped, short-lived and revocable.
Hydration ships data into the page
Props serialized into the HTML (__NEXT_DATA__, the RSC payload) outlive TLS: View Source, saved pages, caches.
Fix: Pass only what the screen needs. Never pass whole records as props. Fetch PII client-side, after consent.
A CDN or ISR cache of a personalized page can serve one customer's data to the next visitor.
Fix: Cache-Control: private, no-store on personalized routes. Keep PII out of static and ISR pages.
Server Components call APIs on the first request, before the consent banner has loaded.
Fix: Gate server fetches on the consent cookie. Defer personalization and tracking until the user agrees.
Any env var with that prefix is baked into client JavaScript at build time (see gap 9).
Fix: Keep secrets server-only. Scan the built bundle for keys in CI before every deploy.
TLS is hop-by-hop on a data bus
The queue, Worker and logs each decrypt the message, and any of them can store it.
Fix: Sign each message (HMAC or Ed25519). Encrypt sensitive fields end to end (JWE). Use mTLS between services.
Anyone who finds the webhook URL can POST a fake or repeated event.
Fix: Verify X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256 on the raw body. Reject stale timestamps. Use idempotency keys.
The webhook table keeps customer data after the event is processed.
Fix: Store IDs, not payloads. Purge processed rows on a schedule. Encrypt the table at rest.
A Shopify Admin token in KV or env grants the whole store if it leaks.
Fix: Least-privilege scopes, short-lived tokens, rotation, and alerts on unusual use.
MuleSoft and SFCC decrypt, transform and can log every payload and connector secret.
Fix: Mask fields in DataWeave, use secure properties, turn off payload logging, encrypt sensitive fields.
The JVM has no in-process sandbox
The Security Manager is deprecated (Java 17), so every dependency runs with full app rights.
Fix: Isolate services, scan dependencies, patch fast. Keep secrets short-lived and out of Strings.
Consent isn't carried with the event
Audiences and conversions reach Google without their ad_user_data / ad_personalization state.
Fix: Attach Consent Mode v2 state at capture. Drop or redact the event when consent is denied.
Timeouts, job re-runs and webhook redelivery create double conversions or records.
Fix: One idempotency key per event, deduped with a TTL. Upsert on stable IDs such as offerId or SKU.
Wasm host imports are the door
A Wasm sandbox is only as tight as the functions the host gives it.
Fix: Grant the fewest imports possible. Shopify Functions grant no network at all.
One kernel bug, --privileged, or a mounted docker.sock hands over the whole host.
Fix: Run as non-root, drop capabilities, use seccomp and a read-only FS. Use gVisor, Kata or a VM for untrusted code.
etcd stores them encoded, not encrypted: anyone with get-secrets or a backup reads them (gap 1).
Fix: Turn on etcd encryption with a KMS provider, lock down RBAC on secrets, or use an external vault.
Pod traffic is plaintext by default
The cluster network is flat: any pod reaches any pod, unencrypted across nodes.
Fix: Default-deny NetworkPolicy. mTLS through a service mesh, or WireGuard in the CNI. Don't auto-mount tokens.
ENV values and copied .env files live in image layers for good, readable with docker history.
Fix: Use build secrets (--secret), scan images in CI, and inject secrets at runtime from a vault.
The host can read VM memory
The hypervisor and cloud operator can see guest RAM, including decrypted PHI and card data.
Fix: Confidential VMs (AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX) for regulated workloads; keys in an HSM or KMS.
Celigo retries, error records and logs hold full payloads outside your own systems.
Fix: Mask sensitive fields in the flow, shorten retention, and confirm the data region and DPA or BAA.
SAP RFC users with wide roles; Magento integration tokens that never expire.
Fix: Least privilege per interface, managed identity and Key Vault on Azure, scheduled rotation.
Magecart injects card skimmers into Magento checkouts, some hidden in SVG onload (gap 3).
Fix: Patch fast. CSP and Subresource Integrity. PCI DSS 4.0 6.4.3 script inventory. Hosted payment fields.
IDoc and EDI flat files wait on SFTP drop folders between runs.
Fix: PGP-encrypt files, delete them after pickup, and move to API or queue delivery where you can.

Base64 changes how data is written, not who can read it. Compiling changes what code can do. TLS protects the wire, not the endpoints. Wasm, containers and VMs limit reach, not readership. Only encryption, server-side authorization and contracts decide who can read data.
